title: Cost-aware rollback orchestrator for safe config applies
creator: Ethan Kim
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a rollout-safe, cost-aware rollback orchestrator that automatically detects harmful config changes (especially around batching, caching, and autoscaling) and performs staged remediations with reconciliation back to a known-good state. The system should prioritize customer-facing SLOs (latency/error-rate) over raw cost reductions, but preserve cost hints for post-mortem recommendations.

Problem background:
- Recent autoscaling/batching experiments showed regressions where aggressive batching reduced cost-per-token but caused 95th percentile latency breaches.
- Current config apply path (apply -> monitor -> manual revert) is slow and error-prone for nights/weekend incidents.
- We need an automated safety net to roll changes back when regressions are detected, with clear guardrails to avoid flapping and accidental oscillation.

Goals:
1) Reliable automatic rollback for config updates that violate SLO or create regressions tied to batching/caching changes.
2) Cost-aware decision logic: rollback only when customer experience is meaningfully degraded or there is clear cross-metric negative impact.
3) Minimal blast radius via staged rollbacks / canary-scoped remediations.
4) Full state reconciliation so the control plane, runtime, and observability artifacts reflect the final state (no half-applied toggles).

Scope (v1):
- Triggers: latency SLO breaches, error-rate increase, throughput drop, sudden CPU/GPU utilization anomalies after a config apply. Also delta in cost-per-token above configurable threshold when coupled with quality regressions.
- Guardrails: minimum traffic window for evaluation, hysteresis windows (config-specific), confidence scoring based on metric magnitude + volume, manual approval override, and automated backoff to a safe variant (e.g., smaller batch size or different quantization profile).
- Reconciliation: capture pre-apply snapshot, record applied diffs, ensure idempotent rollback path, reconcile caches (KV cache prefix validity), and confirm runtime acknowledges the target state.
- Integration: Redwood Console rollout UI, telemetry dashboards, and Optimize suggestion engine (to annotate recommended post-rollback knobs).

Non-goals:
- Rewriting autoscaler logic (we react to symptoms, don't replace scaling policies in v1).
- Fully automated cost-tradeoff negotiation without human-in-the-loop for ambiguous cases.
acceptance_criteria:
1) The orchestrator can detect and automatically roll back a config change in a canary pool when the 95th percentile latency exceeds SLO by configured margin for at least 3 consecutive evaluation windows.
2) Rollback action is logged, a rollback PR is stamped in audit logs, and the console shows pre-apply snapshot + post-rollback confirmation.
3) The system does not rollback changes when only cost decreases but SLOs remain within thresholds; instead it surfaces a recommendation in Optimize.
4) Reconciliation verifies runtime state via a read-after-write confirm step: when rollback completes, runtime reports expected configs and KV cache version matches expected checkpoint.
5) Unit and integration tests cover trigger detection, guardrail hysteresis, staged rollback progression (canary -> region -> global), and an idempotent reconcile run.
design_decisions:
- Use snapshot-diff approach: capture a compact JSON snapshot of config state (apply-time) and store diff so rollbacks can be targeted without full reapply.
- Confidence score calculation composes magnitude * traffic weight * anomaly duration. This avoids noisy short-lived blips.
- Prefer 'staged remediations' rather than immediate global rollback: attempt canary revert, then rollback 10% regions, 50%, then global if necessary. Each stage requires metric re-evaluation.
- Integrate with existing 'Optimize' recommendation engine to push suggestions rather than automatic changes when tradeoffs are ambiguous.
- Implement an explicit 'dry-run' revert mode that performs reconciliation checks without committing changes for high-risk applies.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (incubation): unit tests, local sim harness, and synthetic injection test harness (complete).
Phase 1 (canary): deploy orchestrator to 'canary pools' only; enable automatic rollback for non-production test tenants and an internal production shadow bucket with 2% traffic. Monitor for 7 days. (ETA: 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-10).
Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 10% of production routes with automated rollback but require auto-notify + 1 engineer on-call acknowledgement for cross-metric cases. (ETA: 2026-03-11 -> 2026-03-22).
Phase 3 (global): full rollout with runbook and SLA adjustments; add Optimize integration for post-rollback recommendations.
telemetry_and_alerting:
- Dashboard: Rollback actions by cause (latency/error/cost) over time, average time-to-rollback, per-route SLO breaches attributable to recent config applies.
- Alerts: Pager if rollback occurs in >1 region within 15m OR if rollback count for a single release >3 in 24h.
- Audit logs: attach config diff and snapshot id to every automatic rollback; link to GitHub rollback PR and Confluence incident note.
- Metrics emitted: rollback.initiated (labels: cause, stage, release), rollback.completed (labels: success, duration_ms), reconcile.status (labels: success|partial|failed).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for confidence scoring and trigger thresholds.
- Integration tests: apply -> observed metric injection -> orchestrator should perform expected stage rollbacks.
- Chaos tests: flip network partitions and sim partial apply to ensure reconciliation can recover.
- Load tests: apply large-scale batch-config changes in staging to validate hysteresis and no false positives.
- Post-deploy canary checklist: manual verification steps, runbook rehearsals, and team sign-off.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Design review: Team agreed on staged remediations and snapshot-diff approach. Action: Priya to produce reconciliation checklist.
2026-02-25 - Proto complete: implemented snapshot capture and confidence scorer prototype; ran synthetic latency injection and observed expected canary rollback in simulated environment.
2026-02-28 - Security review onboarded: asked to ensure audit logs are write-once and that KMS policies prevent rollback tampering. Security: Marco Rivera. Action: add HMAC of snapshot id.
2026-03-03 - Code review feedback from Marco Rivera: tighten retry logic in reconcile step, avoid blocking apply path on reconcile failures (fail-open only for non-production applies).
2026-03-07 - Canary deployment started for internal tenants. Observed one rollback triggered by an aggressive batch-size change; rollback executed successfully and reconcile confirmed cache epoch.
2026-03-09 - Found issue: rollback path left stale dispatcher flag in a rare race; hotfix PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7245. Patch merged and deployed to canary.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: extend evaluation window, add additional unit tests for race, schedule runbook tabletop for on-call teams on 2026-03-18.
